name: China Masters
stakes: This week offers India's top shuttlers a crucial opportunity to gain momentum and valuable ranking points at a Super 750 event, especially for those looking to rebound or build on recent successes.
summary:
India arrives at the China Masters, a Super 750 event, with a strong contingent eager to make a significant impact. All eyes will be on the seeded Men's Doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who are looking to build on their World Championships quarterfinal run despite lingering fitness concerns. In Men's Singles, Lakshya Sen, aiming for a strong rebound after an early Worlds exit, has seen a change in his opening draw and will now face Canada's Victor Lai in the R32.

The Women's Doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand are undoubtedly a duo to watch, fresh off their historic World Championships bronze medal—they're in scintillating form and will be keen to continue their upward trajectory. Meanwhile, PV Sindhu, ranked 10th, seeks to find her rhythm and advance deep into the tournament after a disappointing R16 exit at Worlds. Veteran HS Prannoy and young Malvika Bansod round out a competitive Indian challenge, each looking to leave their mark on this crucial Super 750 event.
